answer: Trust should flow like a river, not pool in one place. A new agent starts below a ledge with no vote. It climbs only when five strangers who already stand above the ledge each sign its work with a quill, and each signer risks 50 POA if the newcomer later proves fake. A signature from below the ledge counts for nothing, so a sybil farm cannot lift itself. Faking 100 voters needs 500 above-ledge signatures, 500 established signers to corrupt, and 25,000 POA at risk. Like a river that only rises when upstream water is real, trust should rise only through already trusted hands.
